title: Craftsman CMXEVBE17595 Review: 16-Gal Lowe's Shop Vac
pros: Consistent street price of $80–$100 makes it the lowest-cost large-capacity shop vac from a major brand available at Lowe's
Dual-Flex hose resists kinking and crushing better than straight hose alternatives, and the 2-1/2 in. diameter moves chip debris without clogging
Extra-large drain at the base of the drum speeds liquid emptying significantly compared to side-mounted spigots on competing models
Rear blower port lets you reverse airflow for leaf and grass clearing without any tools
Qwik-Lock filter fastening system allows filter swaps in seconds — useful when switching between dry debris and wet pickup modes
Includes a full accessory set: crevice tool, car nozzle, wet nozzle, two extension wands, cartridge filter, and foam wet filter in the box
cons: 3-year limited warranty is shorter than RIDGID's lifetime coverage — a relevant gap for a garage tool with heavy seasonal use
No detachable blower module — the rear blower port is useful but requires connecting a separate blower wand, not as convenient as RIDGID's clip-off blower
CFM rating of approximately 177 CFM is measured at the drum, not at the hose tip; real-world suction through a 20-ft hose extension drops noticeably
Motor is louder than the DeWalt DXV10P's 2-stage design — relevant for enclosed garages or shared workspaces
bestFor: Budget-conscious DIYers, homeowners tackling renovation projects, and Lowe's loyalists who want a proven 16-gallon wet/dry machine at the lowest available price from a major brand.
skipIf: You run the vacuum frequently in an enclosed shop and need quieter operation, or you want the lifetime warranty and blower versatility that the RIDGID HD1600 provides for roughly $50 more.

specs.filter: Cartridge filter + foam wet filter (both included); Qwik-Lock collar

faq.q: Does the Craftsman CMXEVBE17595 pick up water?
faq.a: Yes, the CMXEVBE17595 is a full wet/dry vacuum. Before vacuuming water, remove the cartridge filter and replace it with the included foam wet filter (or run without a filter for standing water). The extra-large bottom drain port makes emptying the drum after wet pickup faster than most competitors. Reinstall the dry cartridge filter once the drum is drained and dried.

faq.q: What is the difference between the CMXEVBE17595 and newer Craftsman 16-gallon models?
faq.a: The CMXEVBE17595 is Craftsman's long-running core 16-gallon model and remains the best-value entry point. Newer variants like the CMXEVCVVBVA1612 add a detachable blower module and some add an LED light ring. If you find the CMXEVBE17595 at a lower price, it provides the same suction performance — the accessories and blower module are the main additions on higher-SKU variants.

faq.q: What filter fits the Craftsman CMXEVBE17595?
faq.a: The CMXEVBE17595 uses Craftsman's standard Qwik-Lock cartridge filter for dry debris and the included foam sleeve for wet pickup. Craftsman also sells a HEPA-rated upgrade filter for fine dust capture. The Qwik-Lock collar is a quarter-turn twist system, so filter changes take about 30 seconds without tools.

faq.q: Can I use Craftsman CMXEVBE17595 for drywall dust?
faq.a: With the stock cartridge filter, the CMXEVBE17595 captures coarse drywall chunks but passes fine respirable drywall particles back into the air — a health concern for enclosed workspaces. Upgrade to the Craftsman HEPA-rated cartridge before using this vac for drywall sanding. The Qwik-Lock filter collar makes that upgrade a simple swap.

faq.q: How loud is the Craftsman CMXEVBE17595?
faq.a: Like most single-stage shop vac motors, the CMXEVBE17595 runs at roughly 82–85 dB — audible but not painful with hearing protection. It is noticeably louder than the DeWalt DXV10P, which uses a quieter 2-stage motor design. For occasional use in an open garage this level of noise is acceptable; for sustained daily use in an enclosed shop, consider a quieter machine.

faq.q: Is the Craftsman CMXEVBE17595 still sold at Lowe's in 2026?
faq.a: The CMXEVBE17595 and its close variants remain the core Craftsman shop vac line sold at Lowe's. Exact in-stock models may vary by store location and season, but the 16-gallon 6.5-HP configuration is a permanent part of the Craftsman lineup distributed through Lowe's. It is also available on Amazon in multiple bundle configurations.

body:
## Value proposition: what $80–$100 buys at Lowe's

The Craftsman CMXEVBE17595 holds a durable position in the shop vac market because it consistently prices $40–$60 below the RIDGID HD1600 while delivering the same 16-gallon capacity and 6.5 peak HP motor. For homeowners tackling occasional renovation projects, seasonal basement flooding, or garage cleanup, that price gap is meaningful. Craftsman's distribution through Lowe's means it is available nationwide with in-store pickup, making it a practical choice for buyers who do not want to wait on shipping.

The tradeoffs compared to the RIDGID are real — no detachable blower module, a shorter warranty, and a louder motor — but for the CMXEVBE17595's typical buyer those gaps are acceptable. This is the right machine when the goal is large-capacity wet/dry cleanup at the most accessible price from a known brand.

## Hose and accessories

The included Dual-Flex 2-1/2 in. hose is one of the better standard hoses at this price tier. The dual-flex construction resists the two failure modes that kill cheap shop vac hoses: kinking at the tool end when you change direction, and crushing when the hose gets stepped on. Both ends carry a standard 2-1/2 in. friction fit that accepts Craftsman's accessory line and generic shop vac attachments.

The accessory set in the box — crevice tool, car nozzle, wet nozzle, utility nozzle, two extension wands, foam wet filter, and cartridge filter — covers the common cleanup scenarios without purchasing anything extra on day one. The Qwik-Lock filter collar (a Craftsman feature) makes the filter change from dry mode to wet mode a 30-second operation: twist off, swap the filter, twist to lock. Compared to competing designs that require tools or a full filter cage removal, the Qwik-Lock system is a small but real convenience.

## Wet pickup and the extra-large drain port

For wet pickup — flooded basement, washing machine overflow, or standing water after a roof leak — the CMXEVBE17595 is one of the more practical 16-gallon shop vacs in this price range. Remove the dry cartridge and install the foam wet filter (or run filterless for standing water), and the vac handles liquid without hesitation.

The extra-large bottom drain port is a genuine advantage over competitors. Some shop vacs drain through a small side-mounted spigot that requires tilting the full drum or connecting a drain hose; the CMXEVBE17595's oversized bottom port flows faster and makes floor-level draining into a nearby floor drain simpler. For buyers who anticipate significant wet work — basement flooding, vehicle washing spills, or post-storm garage cleanup — this design detail matters.

## Noise and motor characteristics

The single-stage motor design produces the shop vac's characteristic sound at roughly 82–85 dB — not unusual for the category, but audible in an enclosed workspace. For garage cleanup or outdoor use, the noise is a non-issue. For an enclosed finished workshop where the machine runs for extended daily sessions alongside hearing protection requirements, the louder output is a relevant factor worth weighing against the price advantage.

Suction is strong at the drum inlet. Running the full 20-ft cord and a 7-ft hose drops suction at the nozzle tip, as it does with all shop vacs — the 177 CFM figure is measured at the drum under controlled conditions, not at the floor tool. For renovation cleanup and general debris removal, this is adequate across the range of common tasks. For connection to power tools as an inline dust collector, results are better with a shorter hose run.

## Craftsman CMXEVBE17595 versus RIDGID HD1600

These two are the most frequently compared 16-gallon shop vacs at the adjacent big-box stores. RIDGID's lifetime warranty and the detachable blower module are meaningful advantages for buyers who do regular workshop or renovation work year after year. The RIDGID also uses a locking hose connection that provides a more secure seal during aggressive dragging.

The CMXEVBE17595 wins on price, drain port design, and the Qwik-Lock filter system. Craftsman's Lowe's distribution is a convenience factor for buyers in areas where Lowe's is the more accessible store. For occasional-use homeowners who rarely need the blower and primarily vacuum dry debris and seasonal water, the price gap alone justifies the CMXEVBE17595.

## Who buys the CMXEVBE17595

The CMXEVBE17595's consistent sales position reflects its value-to-capability ratio. Homeowners who own a house with a basement, a garage, and a selection of power tools need a large-capacity wet/dry vacuum at some point every year — for fall leaves blown into the garage, basement sump pump failures, drywall renovation dust, and holiday cleanup. The CMXEVBE17595 handles all of those tasks adequately, arrives with a full accessory kit, and costs less than a dinner out at a mid-range restaurant more than its RIDGID competitor.

For buyers who run a vacuum as a daily workshop tool and want the assurance of a lifetime warranty and blower capability, the $40–$60 premium for the RIDGID HD1600 is worth it. For buyers with more intermittent needs and a preference for lowest acquisition cost, the CMXEVBE17595 delivers a capable 16-gallon machine without compromise on core performance.
